subject.name: openssl.blind
subject.format: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, statically linked, stripped
subject.build: gcc, ./Configure no-shared no-docs no-tests -static linux-x86_64, then strip --strip-all

program_level.ioc_verdict: benign; dominated by false positives (ASN.1 OIDs read as IPv4, ASN.1 time strings read as IPv6, assembly attribution URL, charset-table maintainer email, example-certificate domains)

function_identifications.blind_id: error subsystem: records file/line/func into the per-thread error state top slot
function_identifications.source_signature: void ERR_set_debug(const char *file, int line, const char *func)
evidence: exact body match: free+strdup file, set line, free+strdup func

function_identifications.blind_id: error subsystem: clear/advance the top error slot for a new error
error subsystem: record library id and reason code
function_identifications.source_signature: void ERR_set_error(int lib, int reason, const char *fmt, ...)
evidence: called as (0xf=ERR_LIB_CRYPTO, reason, 0) from the malloc-failure path
third of the ERR_new/ERR_set_debug/ERR_set_error raise trio

function_identifications.blind_id: free with pluggable allocator (overridable function pointer, default libc free)
function_identifications.source_signature: void CRYPTO_free(void *str, const char *file, int line)

function_identifications.blind_id: malloc with pluggable allocator; raises a malloc-failure error
function_identifications.source_signature: void *CRYPTO_malloc(size_t num, const char *file, int line)
evidence: overridable global fn-ptr, default libc malloc

function_identifications.source_signature: void *CRYPTO_zalloc(size_t num, const char *file, int line)

function_identifications.surfaced: shared callee of the ERR trio
function_identifications.blind_id: return the per-thread error state structure
stack accessor: return count, or -1 when NULL
evidence: return *p (num at offset 0) or -1 for NULL
very high fan-in typical of the stack primitive

function_identifications.blind_id: openssl speed benchmark subcommand entry point

evidence: four 256-entry table constants flagged as AES S-boxes
MD5 genuinely present (unlike the SQLite case); SHA-1 also present sharing the same first four words (crypto/sha/sha_local.h:60)

scoring_summary.calibration_note: No over-confidence: every identification confirmed, including the lowest-confidence ones (ERR_get_state 80, MD5 80). The model was slightly under-confident, never over-confident.

fixture_promotion.promotion_mechanics_note: The OpenSSL static build is NOT byte-reproducible across toolchains (a CI rebuild produced a different sha256), so the exact 7.9 MiB subject bytes are pinned via Git LFS rather than rebuilt. The promoted integration test (promoted_test) loads that binary (lfs:true checkout), verifies its sha256 against subject.sha256, and asserts the program-level facts + 15 function addresses reproduce against a real Ghidra worker. It is integration-tier (gated by VIVARIUM_INTEGRATION) and runs as an advisory step in .github/workflows/live-regression.yml. build-openssl-fixture.sh is retained for provenance only.
